parole.significato: Synonym of turnip cake (often particularly referring to stir-fried preparation popular in South East Asia)
parole.testo: From Teochew 菜頭粿 /菜头粿 (cai³ tao⁵ guê²) and Hokkien 菜頭粿 /菜头粿 (chhài-thâu-kóe).

parole.significato: To malinger, to skive, to shirk one's duties (especially, military duties) by feigning illness or reporting sick.
parole.testo: From Teochew 臭 (cao³, “dirty, ill-reputed”) + 經 /经 (gêng¹, “to evade; to pass the buck”).

parole.significato: A kind of steamed rice cake originating in Teochew cuisine, served with preserved radish (chai po).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Teochew 水粿 (zui² guê²) or Hokkien 水粿 (chúi-kóe).
Borrowed from Teochew 侯栗 (gao⁶ lag⁸, “chestnut”).
From Teochew 興 /兴 (hêng¹, “fortunate”) or Hokkien 幸 (hēng, “fortunate”). Compare Thai เฮง (heng), Khmer ហេង (heeng), Vietnamese hên.

parole.significato: Phew!, thank goodness; expressing relief, e.g., when an extremely unlucky outcome has been avoided.
parole.testo: From Teochew 興啊 /兴啊 (hêng¹ a⁷) or Hokkien 幸啊 (hēng--a). By surface analysis, heng (“lucky”) + ah (used for emphasis).

parole.significato: Synonym of chao keng (“to malinger, to shirk military duties by reporting sick”).
parole.testo: Clipping of chao keng, from Teochew 臭 (cao³, “dirty, ill-reputed”) + 經 /经 (gêng¹, “to evade; to pass the buck”).

parole.significato: Someone who avoids work, military duties or other responsibilities by constantly reporting sick; a malingerer.
parole.testo: keng + -ster, the first element is a clipping of chao keng, from Teochew 臭 (cao³, “dirty, ill-reputed”) + 經 /经 (gêng¹, “to evade; to pass the buck”).

parole.significato: A Teochew dish of flat rice sheets in a soy sauce broth and an array of braised meats (offal, tongue, rinds, pork belly…
parole.testo: From Teochew 粿汁 (guê² zab⁴). Compare Thai กวยจั๊บ (guai-jáp) / ก๋วยจั๊บ (gǔai-jáp).
From Teochew 米篩目／米筛目 (bhi² tai¹ mag⁸), with the first element reanalyzed as the word mee, meaning “noodles”, from Hokkien 麵／面 (mī).
From Teochew 潮州 (dio⁵ ziu¹). See also Hokkien 潮州 (Tiô-chiu). Doublet of Chaozhou.
